title: Pope Leo comes out swinging against AI slop
key_facts: Pope Leo XIV posted on X urging support for human artists over AI output ('AI slop').

He wrote that there is an 'ontological difference, even before an aesthetic one' between art and what a machine generates through statistical calculation based on millions of images created by others.
He said the Church wishes to renew an alliance with artists and cultural institutions to safeguard humanity.

His 42,300-word encyclical Magnifica Humanitas already called out Big Tech and the AI industry, including dangerous conditions for child and adolescent workers who crush materials from which rare earths are extracted.
Mashable says the topic returned this week after the New York Times reported that Anthropic tried and failed to convince religious leaders that Claude could be a conscious being with moral status.
Mashable puts the number of Catholics at 1.4 billion.
quote_evidence: Algorithms lack the spark of humanity.
In this era of artificial intelligence, it is becoming urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce.
For this reason, the Church wishes to renew an alliance with artists and cultural institutions to safeguard our humanity.
why_it_matters_hint: A high-profile religious leader takes a public stand for human artists against AI-generated content.
event_date: 9 Oct 2026 (Mashable says "this morning"; article stamped 10 Oct 01:48 UTC)
notes: Single outlet reporting a public post; the post itself was not opened.
